title: Popularity Trajectories and Mixing Patterns of Urban Venues in Two European Cities
abstract: arXiv:2610.18917v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Urban venues such as restaurants, shops, bars and parks host the daily life of a city, and their collective rise and fall signals how vibrant a neighbourhood is. The usual assumption is that a venue's fortunes follow its neighbourhood's, so that how wealthy an area is and how many people live there will decide a venue's performance. Yet whether there is a common performance trajectory shared by venues over time is underexplored. In this study, we use 5.5 years of Foursquare data for about 10^4 venues in London and Barcelona. We found six distinguishable shapes recur in both cities, that are (1) Fall, (2) Rise, (3) Rise & Fall, (4) Steady, (5) Ephemeral (an early hit that loses popularity fast) and (6) Underdogs (a slow starter that gains popularity late). translated_title: 两个欧洲城市中城市场所的流行度轨迹与混合模式
translated_abstract: 诸如餐馆、商店、酒吧和公园等城市场所承载着城市的日常生活，它们的集体兴衰反映着一个社区的活力程度。通常的假设是，一个场所的命运紧随其所在社区的命运，因此一个地区的富裕程度和居民数量将决定该场所的表现。然而，场所之间是否随时间共享某种共同的表现轨迹这一问题尚未得到充分探索。在本研究中，我们使用了伦敦和巴塞罗那约10^4个场所长达5.5年的Foursquare数据。我们发现六种可区分的形态在两个城市中反复出现，分别是：(1) 下降型，(2) 上升型，(3) 先升后降型，(4) 稳定型，(5) 昙花一现型（早期走红但迅速失去人气）以及 (6) 后起之秀型（起步缓慢但后期获得人气）。然而，并未出现恢复型形态，即两个城市中都不存在U型的先降后升群体。此外，我们发现贫困剥夺程度和人口密度并不能指示（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 本研究基于伦敦和巴塞罗那约一万个场所5.5年的Foursquare签到数据，发现城市场所的流行度演变可归纳为六种典型轨迹（下降、上升、先升后降、稳定、昙花一现、后起之秀），且不存在U型复苏轨迹，而社区的贫困程度与人口密度并不能预示场所的流行度走向。
en_tdlr: Using 5.5 years of Foursquare data on ~10,000 venues in London and Barcelona, this study identifies six recurring popularity trajectories (Fall, Rise, Rise & Fall, Steady, Ephemeral, and Underdogs), finds no U-shaped recovery pattern in either city, and shows that neighborhood deprivation and population density do not predict a venue's popularity trajectory.
